respond.description: Answer the service that called this workflow's webhook URL, with the status code and body you choose. Without this step the caller gets a 200 as soon as the run starts; with it, the caller waits for your reply (up to a minute), so you can send back a result, a thank-you message, or a 4xx that tells it what was wrong. The run carries on after replying. Reply once per run: a second reply has nobody to go to.
respond.name: respond

parameters.description: The HTTP status to answer with: 200 for success, 201 for something created, 202 for accepted, 400 or 422 to refuse what was sent.
parameters.name: status_code

parameters.description: What to send back: text, or a value from an earlier step. An object or a list is sent as JSON; text is sent as it is. Leave empty to send no body.
parameters.name: body

parameters.description: Extra response headers. Headers that start with X- are sent as they are, and a Content-Type of application/xml or text/xml sends the body as XML. Any other header is left out, and the step says so.
parameters.name: headers

returns.description: Whether the caller got the reply. A caller that had already been answered, or that gave up waiting, can't be replied to; the run carries on either way.

delivered.description: Whether the reply reached the caller.

note.description: What happened, in a sentence, and any headers the reply went without.

status_code.description: The status code that was sent.

description: Start a workflow from any service that can call a URL, with whatever it sends, and reply to it with a status code and a body.

skipflow_webhook_trigger.description: Start the workflow when an outside service calls its webhook URL. Each workflow gets a URL of its own; whatever the service sends (JSON, form fields or text) is on the trigger's variable as body, with the request's headers and query too. Give the trigger the service's signing secret and every call is checked before it starts a run. Add the Reply to the caller step to answer the call with your own status code and body.

parameters.description: The secret the sender signs each call with (an HMAC-SHA256 of the body, as hex or base64, with or without a sha256= prefix, or Stripe-style t=...,v1=...), or a fixed token it sends as-is. Write @secrets.NAME to use a workspace secret. Leave empty to accept every call to the URL.
parameters.name: secret

parameters.description: The header the signature or token arrives in, such as X-Hub-Signature-256 or Authorization. Leave empty to look in the usual ones.
parameters.name: signature_header
